goal: Replace axios-blob (responseType:'blob' + URL.createObjectURL) downloads for calibration/weighting (+ formato4/tags pairs) with: request a signed download URL, then native browser navigation, so the browser streams to disk with native progress instead of buffering a Blob in page memory.
design_decisions: Contract mirrors JAA-757 backend exactly: GET .../download-url (existing api instance, header auth) -> {url, expires_in}; GET .../download-signed?token=... is the URL the browser navigates to directly (window.location.assign) — no axios, no responseType:blob, no createObjectURL.

mock-server: added mock-server/lib/download-tokens.js (issue/validate, same resource-binding semantics as the backend) + download-url/download-signed routes in mock-server/routes/calibration.js and mock-server/routes/weighting.js, reusing the existing zip/csv-building logic.
api.ts: downloadCalibrationReport / downloadWeightingCSV rewritten to call the *-download-url endpoint then window.location.assign(url) instead of GET .../download with responseType:'blob'.

Scope: ac3 names downloadCalibrationReport/downloadWeightingCSV '(y pares)' explicitly; downloadFormato4/downloadTagTableCSV/downloadTagZip/downloadEligibilityFile are NOT touched here (no corresponding backend download-url endpoint shipped in JAA-757) — left on the existing blob pattern, noted as follow-up scope if desired.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: downloadCalibrationReport / downloadWeightingCSV no longer use responseType:'blob' or URL.createObjectURL; they navigate to a signed URL instead. npm test + lint + typecheck green; Playwright walkthrough triggers the download.
acceptance_criteria.how_to_verify: npm test && npm run lint && npx tsc -b; grep -L "responseType: ['\"]blob" for these two fns; Playwright e2e drives a calibration/weighting download and asserts navigation (no blob fetch).
